summary_sentence: For example, a three-word address names one specific 3 m × 3 m square of the Earth's surface — a front door, a gate, a tent peg — in words a human can say, hear and remember.

examples.label: Example · The square is the unit

body.t: 57 trillion squares of 3 m × 3 m tile the planet (land and sea alike). A word address does not name a building or a person — it names one of those squares, and the building is a separate fact.

The system deliberately places confusable word combinations far apart, so a mishearing lands obviously wrong rather than next door — the design answer to the spoken-address problem, explained here because it shapes how carefully you should still read codes back.

faq: Can this page look up any three words officially?

Official conversion between words and coordinates is what3words' own service, delivered through their app and licensed API. This helper explains the system and supports the surrounding workflow; it does not impersonate their API.

The English list uses about 40,000 words; three-word combinations from it name the 57 trillion squares. Other languages have their own lists, and addresses do not translate word-for-word between them.
Deliberately not: memorable, common words go to populated places, confusables are separated by distance, and offensive words are excluded — curation is the system's real product.
Many UK and international emergency services accept word addresses because callers often cannot give anything better. If you send one, read it back slowly — and give coordinates too when you can.
Word address or postcode for a delivery?
Postcodes find the street; a word square finds the door, gate or dock on it. Couriers increasingly accept both — the square wins where doors outnumber addresses.
Can I invent my own three words for my house?
No — the assignments are fixed by the system. Your square already has its words; the official app tells you them.
The system operator controls the list; addresses are stable by design intent, but the guarantee is a company's, not mathematics' — the honest difference from open codes.
